ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the picture there are five bowls labeled Q, R, S, T, Z. In bowl Q there are two triangles and one square; in bowl R there are two circles and one square; in bowl S there is one triangle and two squares; in bowl T there is one circle and two squares; in bowl Z there is one triangle, one circle, and one square. The problem states that Q, R, S, T have already been arranged by weight from light to heavy, among which Q is the lightest and T is the heaviest. Reasoning: Let the weights of the triangle, circle, and square be a, b, c respectively. From Q being lighter than R, we can get 2a + c < 2b + c, therefore a < b, that is, the triangle is lighter than the circle. The weight of Z is a + b + c, and the weight of Q is 2a + c, so Z - Q = b - a > 0, indicating that Z is heavier than Q. The weight of R is 2b + c, so R - Z = b - a > 0, indicating that Z is lighter than R. Therefore Z should be placed between Q and R.

raw_record.question_text: Karin wants to place five bowls on a table so that they are ordered according to their weight. She has already placed bowls Q, R, S, and T in order, where Q is lightest and T is heaviest. Where should bowl Z be placed relative to the other bowls?

method.method_draft: Read the contents of each pictured bowl as combinations of three object types: Q contains two triangles and one square; R contains two circles and one square; S contains one triangle and two squares; T contains one circle and two squares; Z contains one triangle, one circle, and one square. From the text, use that Q, R, S, T are already in increasing weight order, with Q lightest and T heaviest. Let the triangle, circle, and square weights be a, b, and c. Since Q < R, 2a + c < 2b + c, so a < b: a triangle is lighter than a circle. Compare Z to Q and R: Z = a + b + c, Q = 2a + c, so Z - Q = b - a > 0, hence Z is heavier than Q. Also R = 2b + c, so R - Z = b - a > 0, hence Z is lighter than R. Therefore Z must be placed between bowls Q and R.
